lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ember Keep rises out of the ash, black against a sky the colour of a forge. Ash falls like snow, and the whole fortress glows red from within.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At the broken gate stands a knight in black armour, alone, as he has stood for a hundred years. His sword is planted point down before him.

lines.speaker: halvard
lines.text: Good evening. I am Halvard, captain of the Warden guard. I hold this gate for the Keeper.
lines.direction: deep and hollow inside the helm; old-fashioned courtesy

lines.speaker: halvard
lines.text: You carry embers. I can feel them from here, like summer. I regret that I cannot let them pass.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: Halvard. You used to let me win at draughts. No. You used to let him win.
lines.direction: suddenly old and slow, Oswin's cadence, not a child's, then a child, confused

lines.speaker: halvard
lines.text: Child. Where did you learn to say my name like that?

options.label: Why do you still hold the gate?
You swore an oath. So did I. Let's talk about what an oath is for.
The fire behind you made my family what we are. I want to see it.

lines.speaker: halvard
lines.text: Because the Keeper bade me hold it until he released me, and he has not. He does not leave the archive. He speaks to no one but me.

lines.speaker: halvard
lines.text: I love him. I have not forgiven him. Both are still true after a century, which surprises me.
lines.direction: the courtesy slipping, just for a moment

lines.speaker: halvard
lines.text: An oath is for keeping. I have kept mine longer than any oath was meant to be kept. That is not the same as it being right.

lines.speaker: halvard
lines.text: You understand, then. I cannot step aside. I can only be relieved.

lines.speaker: halvard
lines.text: So it reached that far. I am sorry for it. The red came after the Fall. Before, it burned gold, and it was very beautiful, and it was a lie.

lines.speaker: halvard
lines.text: Choose, then. I would rather you turned back. If you will not, I shall try, very politely, to kill you.

options.label: Fight our way past.
Ask the Keeper to release him.

lines.speaker: halvard
lines.text: Then you honour me. On guard.
lines.direction: something like relief

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He fights like a man who has practised every morning for a hundred years, because he has. The ash whirls around the blades.

lines.speaker: halvard
lines.text: A message? I may carry a message. That is within my oath. What shall I tell him?

options.label: Tell him we know he tried to put it out.
Tell him the child remembers the hand that stopped him.

lines.speaker: halvard
lines.text: You know that. Nobody knows that. Wait here, if you would be so kind.
lines.direction: very quiet

lines.speaker: halvard
lines.text: The hand. He has asked himself whose hand for a hundred years. Wait here, if you would be so kind.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He goes in. For a long while there is only the falling ash and the red glow. Then a voice speaks from a high window, dry and very old.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Halvard. You have held long enough. Longer than I had any right to ask. I release you.
lines.direction: dry and cold; a long silence before he speaks

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Halvard comes back through the gate slowly, like a man walking out of a long winter. He stops before you and bows.

lines.speaker: halvard
lines.text: Thank you. I had forgotten what it is to want to go somewhere. Be gentle with him. He has been alone a long time.
lines.direction: warm for the first time; the hollowness going

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the black armour goes grey, and then to ash, and the ash falls with all the rest. The gate of Ember Keep stands open.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Come up. Bring the child. I would like to hear about the hand.
lines.direction: a scholar's warmth breaking through, then smothered

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When at last he falls, he goes to one knee first, and sets his sword down carefully, the way a guest sets down a cup.

lines.speaker: halvard
lines.text: Well struck. Tell the Keeper I held. Tell him I held it as long as I could.
lines.direction: faint, still perfectly polite

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When you kneel beside him, the black armour is empty. The gate of Ember Keep stands open.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Warden Archive climbs the inside of a tower, shelf over shelf: three hundred years of the Vale, written where no fire was ever allowed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At a desk beneath the only window sits a figure in a Keeper's robes, all bone and parchment, writing. He does not look up.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: I am Oswin Hale. I remember every year of the Vale's history. You have no idea how heavy that is.
lines.direction: dry, precise, very old

options.label: Halvard fell at the gate. He asked us to tell you he held.
Halvard went gladly. He asked us to be gentle with you.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: He would. He would say exactly that. I should have released him eighty years ago. I wanted someone to talk to.
lines.direction: a long silence; the pen stops

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Sit down. You have killed my only friend and come to ask me questions. I will answer them. That is what I am for.
lines.direction: cold

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Gentle. He was always telling me to be gentle. I was never any good at it. He was the gentle one, under all that iron.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Sit. You gave him back to himself. I owe you the truth, and I have kept it a very long time.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Four hundred years ago the Vale was cold and starving. Seven people climbed the Greywall looking for anything that would keep their children alive.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: They found a fire on the other side. It was not offered to them. They took it, and they ran home, and they called it a gift.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: The Vale was warm for three hundred years, and paid for every hearth in memory. You know that part. You have read it.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: A Keeper learned the price two centuries ago, and buried it in the Sunscar. You found his ledger. We went on selling shards anyway.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: When I was made Keeper I read it too. I swore I would never touch the fire, and I never have. It is why I remember.
lines.direction: the warmth breaking through as anger

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: On the last night, I tried to end it. I was nearly done. And someone stopped my hand.
lines.direction: very long pause before the last words

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Ask what you came to ask. I have had a hundred years to prepare the answers.

options.label: Mother Skarrow's song says the same. The seven came back running.
The church's oldest scripture says it too. The fire we carried out of the burning country.
Old Maud saw that night. Let me check your story against hers.
The crypt named Celandine Marrowby. She fled with a chest of shards.
Do you know the last verse of the Song of the Seven?
Corvin Ashby has read your letters all his life.
Pip, tell him about the hand.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: The goblins kept it. Of course they did. They never used the fire, so it never ate their songs. We should have listened to them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You read the old words aloud. Oswin mouths them with you, word for word, from a memory no fire has ever touched.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Carried, not given. Your church has known for two hundred years. Tell your Mother Aubrine, or don't. That one is yours to choose.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You set his account against Maud's, line by line. The red sky. The ember coming down like a thrown stone. A hooded figure on the hill.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It matches. Maud never touched the fire either. Two people in the Vale who truly remember that night, and they agree.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Maud is alive? She would have been a child, on the riverbank. Tell her I am sorry she had to see it.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Celandine. Nineteen, and frightened, and fast. I saw her run with the chest. I let her go. I thought someone should get out with something.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: She doesn't remember? No. She wouldn't. She will have lit a great many lamps since then.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: The last verse. Yes. They stopped singing it on purpose.
lines.direction: a long silence, then like a man reading from very far away

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Seven went over, and seven came home, with a fire on their backs that was never their own. Pay it back, children, or pay what you've known.
lines.direction: spoken, not sung, but you can hear the tune under it

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Two centuries lost, and now it's yours to sing. Lark would weep to hear it.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Ashby? There was an Ashby who copied for us when I was young. Clever hands. Couldn't spell.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Bring him, after. Whatever happens. Someone should have all of this who isn't dead.
lines.direction: the warmth getting through before he can stop it

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Pip stands in front of the desk. Oswin looks at her for the first time, and his pen stops.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: You were nearly done. It was quiet. And then a hand came over your shoulder, cold, and pulled yours back.
lines.direction: suddenly old and slow, Oswin's cadence, not a child's

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Yes. That is exactly how it was. Child, how do you have that?
lines.direction: barely audible

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: The fire gave it to me. I think it gave me lots of you. I'm sorry. I didn't ask for it.
lines.direction: a child again

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: No. Nobody asked. That has always been the trouble with it.
lines.direction: a long silence, then softer than he has been in a century

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Whose hand. Did you see?
lines.direction: cold again, very quiet

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: A hood. That's all. A hood, and a voice that said, not like this.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Somewhere among the shelves, in a shadow the red light doesn't reach, someone sighs.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Hooded Stranger steps out from between the shelves, as if they had always been there. Perhaps they had.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: Not like this. Yes, I did say that. I'm surprised anyone kept it.
lines.direction: quiet, faintly amused, faintly sad

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: You.
lines.direction: almost nothing, a breath

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: Me. A hundred years ago I stopped your hand. You were about to put it out, and a fire that has gone out can never go home.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: I want it carried back over the Greywall, to where it was taken from. That's all I have ever wanted. Everything else was waiting.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: The Keep fell. The Vale burned in five places. Children died in the Sunscar. You did that, so a fire could go home?
lines.direction: cold fury, very quiet

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: I did that. I didn't know it would shatter. I'm not asking you to forgive it. I'm asking what happens next.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: Ask what you like. I'll answer what I can.

options.label: Who are you?
Your people supply the Ash Market. The shards that burn the wrong colour.
You knew me the moment you saw me. You know where I'm from.
My people came into the Vale looking for this fire. Is it theirs?
You've watched Pip since the day you came. Why?
Enough. We have embers to carry.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: Someone who was here before, and will be here after. That isn't an answer. I know. It's the one I'm allowed to give.
lines.direction: amused

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: You're asking the right questions. You're only asking them a little early.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: You noticed the colour. Good. Those shards came a long way, and they don't eat. Sell that to whoever you like. Most won't believe you.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: I knew you. You stand in a doorway the way your people do. If the fire goes home, so can you.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: That is nearly the right question. Not quite. Ask me again one day, on the other side of the wall.
lines.direction: a long pause, almost pleased

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: Because she carries the night I'm most ashamed of, and I wanted to know if it hurt her. It does. I'm sorry for that, too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Far below, the whole tower shudders. The red light in the window flares, and somewhere beneath the Keep something enormous breathes in.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: The Kindled. Sorrel is in the flame hall. She is feeding it.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: Then we can finish arguing afterwards. I'll stand with you for this part, at least.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Hall of the Flame is vast and round, its walls leaning inward like hands cupped around a candle. At its heart the flame burns red.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Coiled around it, scales like banked coals, sleeps a red dragon. Every breath it takes stirs the ash across the floor.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Before the flame stands Maren Sorrel. Behind her a line of the Kindled faithful wait in their best clothes, holding hands.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: You came. I hoped you would. You've carried the embers further than I ever could. Now help me finish it.
lines.direction: warm, quiet, a preacher's rhythm

options.label: Ivo isn't coming. He's done with you.
We have Ivo's notes. He isn't coming.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: I know. He wrote to me. He said he'd had his minute, and it was enough. I'm glad for him, truly. Not everyone gets a minute.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: I know. You left him sitting with a dead woman in the cold. I'm not the only one here who weighs lives, am I?

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Every one of these people chose this. Eleven lives, and the flame burns again, and ten thousand children are warm this winter.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: My mother's kitchen had blue tiles. Or that was someone else's mother. It doesn't matter. Someone's mother had blue tiles.
lines.direction: losing the thread for a moment, then finding it

options.label: Talk to the faithful, not to her. Get them out of the line.
This hall isn't a hearth, Maren. It's a cage. I've seen the plans.
We won't let you feed it, Maren.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You speak to the woman at the end of the line, who is shaking, and to the boy beside her. One by one, hands let go.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: No. Please. Don't listen to them. You'll be cold. Your children will be cold.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So Maren goes herself. She plunges both hands into the heart of the flame, and the red light roars up the walls.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They don't hear you. They hear Maren, and the cold, and their children. The first of them steps forward into the light, and is gone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The flame roars up the walls, red as a wound.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Maren hesitates for a breath. You can see the joints in the walls now, all leaning in. The lock is in the floor, under the dragon.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: A cage keeps things in. That's all I want. Warmth, kept in, for us.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Then I'm sorry. I'll remember you. I remember everyone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She lifts her hand. The first of the faithful steps forward into the light, and is gone, and the flame roars up the walls.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Around the flame, the dragon opens one eye. It is the colour of the fire, and it has waited a century to be warm enough to wake.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The dragon lies still at last, a hill of cooling coal across the floor. The circle is broken. The faithful who are left weep in the ash.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The heart of the flame burns low and gold, like a hearth at the end of an evening. The red is going out of it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Maren Sorrel sits on the steps before it, her hands blackened, looking at them as if they belonged to someone else.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: I can't find my name. I know hundreds of names. Which one was mine?
lines.direction: lost, not pleading

options.label: You're Maren Sorrel. You preached in the hungry towns.
Let me see to her hands.
Leave her. The embers are waiting.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Maren. That's a good name. I think I would have liked her. Did she do much harm?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody answers. She nods, as if someone had.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You clean and bind her hands. She watches, curious, like a child being shown something. The burns will heal. The rest will not.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Her hands are past what you can do. Without a word, Oswin tears a strip from his own robe and binds them for her.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You leave her on the steps. One of the faithful sits down beside her and holds her shoulder, and she lets him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You set down the embers you have carried across the Vale. One by one they flare and lean towards the heart, like people finding each other in a crowd.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: For the first time in a hundred years the Hearthflame is nearly whole. Now someone has to decide what it is for.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Before anyone can speak, the air in the hall turns green and gold and smells of marsh water. Someone has come a very long way.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Little flames. The Court owes you a favour, and the Court pays its debts.
lines.direction: soft and unhurried; a pause before 'little flames', as if tasting it

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In her cupped hands she carries the Mirewood ember. Already the edges of her are thinning, like mist in the morning.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Without it, I will stop. I find I would like to see how this ends first. That is a very mortal wish. You taught it to me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She sets it down with the others, and stays, faint and bright, to watch.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The embers burn together in the Hall of the Flame. The heat of them is like a summer you only half remember.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: I made this choice once, for everyone, alone. I was wrong to make it alone. So. This time it is yours.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Put it out, and the Vale is cold, and it remembers. I will finish what I began, and go with it. I find I would like that.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: Or carry it home, over the Greywall, where it was taken from. I'll walk with you. The Vale will be cold, and it will remember too.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Or light it. Let them be warm. Let them forget a little. Is a memory worth more than a child who isn't hungry?
lines.direction: half lost, but the conviction still there

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: Whatever you pick, I'll still have him in here, and all the others. So you don't have to pick for me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The flame waits. It has waited four hundred years to be asked.

options.label: Pip, what do you want?
I'll speak for Emberwick. They would want to be warm, and to know the price.
If we carry it, I can open the cage without breaking what's inside.
If we take it home, I'm going home too.
We're ready to vote.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: I want Bree to remember Ned. I want the goblin children to eat. I want it to stop eating people. I don't know which one that is.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: I don't think grown-ups know either. You just have to pick, and be sorry properly.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You speak for the town that sent you: Bree's hearth, Tobin's forge, the cooling fields. The hall listens as if Emberwick itself were here.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You trace the lock in the floor with your hands. Built to hold, never to open. But the masons who built it left their key in the stone.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: Yes. I won't pretend it's a warm welcome waiting for you. But it is home.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every hand in the party moves at once. Whatever you choose, the Vale will live with it.

options.label: Rekindle it.
Return it over the Greywall.
Let it die.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You push the embers together. The Hearthflame catches, roars, and settles into a gold so bright it hurts to look at.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Then I will keep it. I have never touched it. Someone in the Vale ought to remember what it costs.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: So it burns again. Someone will notice. I'll be waiting when they do.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You lift the Hearthflame from its cage. It is lighter than you feared, and it leans towards the mountains, like a dog that knows the way home.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: Thank you. I have waited a long time to say that to someone.
lines.direction: for once, plainly glad

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Go, then. I will open the Archive. If the Vale is going to remember, it will want something to read.

lines.speaker: oswin_hale
lines.text: Thank you. Stand back. I know how this goes now. I have had a century to practise it in my head.
lines.direction: the warmth breaks through, and this time he lets it

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He lays his hands on the flame, the hands that never touched it, and it goes down like a lamp. Nobody stops him.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: Then it can never go home. I hope you were right. I do hope you were.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The last ember gutters and goes out. Oswin Hale, Warden-Keeper, goes out with it, and the hall is dark, and cold, and very quiet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That winter the fields of the Vale grow warm again. The frost lifts from the Ashen Ford, and Emberwick's granaries are full by midwinter.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Hearths are lit from the Keep's new fire. Lamps glow in every window. And slowly, so slowly that nobody notices, the Vale begins to forget.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Sit. Eat. Warmest winter of my life, and I've the soup to prove it.
lines.direction: brisk, cheerful, working as she talks

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: I'm still writing Ned down, every night. Some nights I read it back and I don't know who it's about.
lines.direction: softening without slowing down

options.label: We'll tell the Vale what the fire costs.
We'll keep the secret. Let them be warm.
I'll write it all down, where the fire can't reach it.
I'll tell Mother Aubrine what her oldest scripture says.
I'll tell Emberwick where the Marrowby fortune came from.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You tell them. Some believe you. Some light their lamps anyway, and say a warm child is worth a forgotten song. Perhaps they're right.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You keep the secret, as the Wardens did. It sits in you like a coal. Every time someone lights a lamp, you know what it is eating.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You write it in ink, by candle, never by ember-light. Corvin reads every page and copies it twice. It will outlast you both.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mother Aubrine listens without a word. Next morning she preaches a sermon about debts, and the chapel has never been so quiet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lady Celandine hears it out with a smile, under a hundred ember-lamps. By the end of the week she no longer remembers you told her.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Up in Ember Keep, a dead Keeper tends a living fire, and writes down everything the Vale forgets.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You leave Ember Keep at dawn with the Hearthflame in a Warden's iron lantern, and the Hooded Stranger walking ahead towards the Greywall.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Behind you the Vale goes cold. Frost on the Ashen Ford. The warm fields turn to ordinary mud. The hearth shards dim, one by one.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Ned sang flat. He burned the bread. He laughed like a goose. I remember. I remember all of it.
lines.direction: stopping mid-task, for once

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Go on, then. Go and give it back. I'll burn wood. We managed before the fire, and we'll manage after it.

options.label: I'll carry the lantern. Nobody sees what a river hand doesn't want seen.
I'm going home. I don't know yet what that means.
Before we go, I'll tell Emberwick where the Marrowby fortune came from.
We'll come back, if we can.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You wrap the lantern in oilcloth and carry it the way you carried cargo past the Ash Market's lanterns. No one on the road ever knows what passed them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The fire in the lantern leans towards the mountains, and so, you realise, do you. You have always been walking this way.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You tell them. In her cold hall Lady Celandine hears it, and for the first time in a hundred years she remembers the night she ran.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody has crossed the Greywall and come back. Then again, nobody has ever carried the fire home before.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At the foot of the Greywall the Stranger stops, and looks back at the Vale, and for a moment seems almost young.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: Last chance to turn back. No? Good. I would have missed the company.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The first true winter in four hundred years comes down on the Vale. The warm fields freeze. The ford stops steaming.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And all across the Vale, people wake in the night with things they had lost: a song, a face, the way home.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Ned whistled through his teeth when he was nervous. Did I ever tell you? I don't need the book for that any more. I remember.
lines.direction: stopping mid-task, for once

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Sit. Eat. It's going to be a long winter, and we'll need everyone's hands for it.

options.label: I'll go up to the Archive with Corvin. Someone has to write it down.
I'll tell Mother Aubrine. Her flock needs her more than ever.
I'll stand the ford watch with Dagna again.
We'll help Emberwick through the winter.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You and Corvin read for weeks by candle. Halfway along the third shelf he laughs out loud. Forty-one missing years, and here they all are.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mother Aubrine reads the old scripture once, closes it, and opens her chapel to everyone who is cold. Her faith was in the people, then.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You and Dagna walk the frozen bridge at night, two lanterns and no fire. For the first time since the goblins came, she sleeps through till morning.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You chop wood, mend roofs and carry grain. It isn't heroic. It is the work that keeps people alive once the fire is gone.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: He's still in here. Oswin. He isn't tired any more. I think I'll keep him. Somebody should.
lines.direction: suddenly old and slow, Oswin's cadence, not a child's, then her own voice again

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the Skarrow hills the clan eats well that winter, on Emberwick's grain and the warm valley's harvest.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Warm again. Good for the children. But watch. In ten winters you valley folk will forget you owe us grain.
lines.direction: cracked and dry, slow valley tongue

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: We never used your fire, so we will remember for you. Somebody has to sing it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Skarrow clan never came back to the ford after their chief died on the bridge. The warm years didn't bring them down from the hills.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Emberwick forgets them, slowly, the way it forgets everything now. The clan does not forget Emberwick.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: The bridge is open. Nobody tolls it. I'd like to say it was worth it. Some days I can.
lines.direction: low and flat

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The cold comes down hard. Mother Skarrow brings her clan down to the ford, and Emberwick opens its granaries, because a deal is a deal.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Cold again, like the old songs. Now you valley folk learn what we know. Sit. We will teach you how to winter.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: With the cold, the hill clans come down hungry. The Skarrow come to the ford again, and this time nobody goes up the hill to talk.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: They remember the bridge. So do I. That's the trouble with remembering. It works on both sides.
lines.direction: low and flat

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That first hard winter, the Skarrow clan and Emberwick share one granary, and argue over it, loudly, every single week.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Neighbours. That is your word for people you shout at and still feed. Good. We will be neighbours.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: Six years I hid the cold so nobody would leave. Now everyone can see it, and nobody has. I should have trusted them.
lines.direction: quiet, a little hoarse

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The goblin clans come down out of the frozen hills with spears, and the Skarrow come first. They remember who killed their chief.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: I'll go up and talk to them myself. I should have done it on the first day. I have to try, at least once.
lines.direction: a man who has given too many speeches, giving none

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Vorga goes home to his grandmother's fire. His Host breaks up into families again.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: She made me carry water for a month. A month! A warlord! Tell nobody you spared me. No. Tell everybody.
lines.direction: loud, then oddly shy

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Vorga goes home to a clan with no grandmother left in it. He leads them now. He remembers who spared him, and who did not.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: She would have bargained with you. So I will try. It tastes wrong in my mouth. I will try anyway.
lines.direction: no swagger left, only the anger, held carefully

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the night she heard about her grandson, Mother Skarrow sat at her fire and sang nothing at all.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The truce with Emberwick holds, thin as ice on a pond. Everyone walks carefully.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Of Mother Skarrow's line, nobody is left. The Host scattered into the canyons, and the hills have no one to speak for them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Somewhere in the Sunscar, goblins still sing a song about a bridge, and what the valley folk did there.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the spring Ivo Rime opens a surgery in Emberwick, above the bakery. He charges nothing, and he never uses fire.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: Sit down. No, there. You've walked a long way to see me. I can tell from your boots.
lines.direction: soft, tired, a little less tired than he was

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: I had a minute. Most people never get one. I'd like to give a few of them a little longer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody sees Ivo Rime below the snowline again. Pilgrims say a cold light still burns in the tower above the pass.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They say there are two figures at the window, side by side, very still. Nobody climbs up to ask.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At the broken gate of Ember Keep stands an empty suit of black armour, set upright by someone who knew how. Its sword is planted point down.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Travellers bow to it as they pass. Nobody quite knows why. It only seems polite.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At the broken gate there is nothing now but ash, and, every spring, flowers. Pip planted them. She says he liked the yellow ones.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: He let me win at draughts. Well. He let Oswin win. It's the same thing, sort of.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The one who paid the Court still has a gap where a memory used to be. In the warm years, the rest of the Vale slowly grows gaps to match.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It's lonely, being the first. It gets less lonely every year. That is the worst part.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When the fire leaves, the Vale remembers what it lost. All but one memory: the one the Court ate. The Court gives nothing back.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You still can't remember it. But you remember giving it, and why. It was yours to give, and it bought the road home.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: All over the Vale, people wake remembering. The one who paid the Court wakes too, reaches for the old memory, and finds the gap still there.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Court ate it, and the Court gives nothing back. You gave it to carry the fire here, and here is where the fire ended.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mirewood never forgets the trick you played. Every year on the same night, a small light comes to the edge of the marsh and says your names.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Clever little flames. The Court is still deciding whether to admire you. It may take a few hundred years.
lines.direction: amused, and not entirely safe

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mirewood is quieter now. There are fewer lights in the water. On still nights the reeds whisper about a fey who chose to see an ending.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: Bree says when I'm big I'll forget things too, like everybody. That's all right. I've got spares. I'll keep them for whoever needs them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Vale is warm, and fed, and forgetting. What it owes the people who come after is written down somewhere. Whether they read it is up to them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And far beyond the Greywall, something that lost a fire four hundred years ago lifts its head, and sees the light.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In Emberwick, a girl in three scarves stands on the cold bank of the ford and waves until there is nothing left to wave at.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Vale gave back what it took. Whatever it owes now, it will pay in firewood and honest work, and it will remember every bit of it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the far side of the Greywall the wind smells of smoke, and the road goes on. The rest of it is another story.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It is a hard winter. Not everyone sees the spring. The dead of Frostpeak walk further down the valley than ever, and that will need answering too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But in spring the children of Emberwick plant cold ground, and their grandparents tell them stories that are finally true.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Vale let the fire go. What it owes the people after it now is the truth, and a good spring. It is enough to be going on with.
